question: Prediction of progression from MCI to Alzheimer's disease/dementia among ADNI MCI patients, from neuropsychological test scores and structural MRI (FreeSurfer) measures with demographics. The clinical/cognitive and MRI channels are shared; P-156 adds CSF and APOE4. The horizon (fixed 2 years vs latest diagnosis), cohort construction, input representation and validation design differ, which condition 1 allows. Both draw on ADNI 1/GO/2, so the samples overlap (non-independent).

figures.P-168: Longitudinal LSTM (five visits): AUC 0.93 +/- 0.06, a mean and SD over 10 CV folds, not an interval. n=347 (77 converters, 270 non-converters). Hanley-McNeil: Q1=A/(2-A), Q2=2A^2/(1+A), SE=sqrt[(A(1-A)+(76)(Q1-A^2)+(269)(Q2-A^2))/(77*270)] = 0.0206 -> 0.890-0.970 (fold-SD t-interval 0.93 +/- 2.262*0.06/sqrt(10) -> 0.887-0.973). Single-timepoint random forest (index exam only): AUC 0.90 +/- 0.09; Hanley-McNeil SE 0.0242 -> 0.853-0.947 (fold-SD t-interval 0.836-0.964).
figures.P-156: Ensemble Integration, baseline data only: held-out test AUC 0.81 (test set = 841-672 = 169). No interval printed and the test class split is in a supplement not held; with the cohort's 34% progressors (about 58/111), Hanley-McNeil SE 0.0377 -> 0.736-0.884 (0.732-0.888 across splits from 50/119 to 66/103).

matched_figure_check: P-168 reports a single-timepoint model, the input representation P-156 uses: AUC 0.90. P-156's 0.81 lies outside P-168's single-timepoint interval (0.853-0.947 by Hanley-McNeil; 0.836-0.964 from the fold SD), and P-168's 0.90 lies outside P-156's derived interval (0.736-0.884). The matched figure narrows the gap from 0.12 to 0.09 but does not reconcile it. Neither paper reports the other's horizon. P-168's age-restricted single-timepoint AUCs (0.89 over 65, 0.87 over 70) are subsets that do not match P-156's cohort (median age 73.5); the over-70 figure would fall inside P-156's derived interval, which shows the margin is not large.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: no figure reaches 0.97 (0.93, 0.90, 0.81). Both are internal validations (P-168 10-fold CV, n=347; P-156 random 20% hold-out, n=841).

candidate_explanations.difference: Horizon: P-168 predicts conversion within a fixed 2 years of a month-24 index exam; P-156 predicts the latest recorded diagnosis with no fixed horizon, so it includes late converters.
candidate_explanations.quote: The index exam is deﬁned as the exam at 24-month, and the outcome is deﬁned as the progression from MCI to AD before 48-month.

candidate_explanations.difference: Horizon (P-156 side): outcome is the most recent diagnosis.
candidate_explanations.quote: The most recent diagnosis given to each patient (Final DX) was the outcome predicted (stable MCI or progressed to dementia).

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort construction: P-168 keeps only participants with complete NP and MRI data at five visits who were still MCI at month 24, and drops 187 with undetermined status at month 48; P-156 takes all 841 baseline EMCI/LMCI patients.
candidate_explanations.quote: restricted to participants who had corresponding NP tests and MRI measures collected at ﬁve time points (baseline, 6, 12, 18, and 24-month) and were diagnosed with MCI at 24-month (n = 553).

candidate_explanations.difference: Input timepoint and representation: P-168's headline uses five visits; even its single-timepoint model uses the month-24 exam of people already MCI for up to two years, not the first MCI visit. P-168 shows longitudinal input adds 0.03 (0.93 vs 0.90), which accounts for only part of the gap.
candidate_explanations.quote: signiﬁcantly higher mean AUC (0.93 ± 0.06) than the random forest model based on the data collected at a single time point (24-month) (0.90 ± 0.09) (DeLong test P = 0.039).

candidate_explanations.difference: Baseline-only input and feature loss: P-156 uses baseline data only and dropped PET and DTI modalities for missingness.
candidate_explanations.quote: This resulted in several imaging modalities, namely FDG PET, AV45 PET, AV1451 PET and DTI, being removed

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation design: 10-fold CV mean (P-168) vs a single random 20% held-out test set (P-156).
candidate_explanations.quote: performed using two separate 10-fold cross-validation procedures for hyperparameter selection and model performance evaluation.

candidate_explanations.difference: Label and case mix: AD (P-168) vs dementia (P-156); 35.4% of P-156's cohort is early MCI at baseline.
candidate_explanations.quote: Our cohort derived from TADPOLE consisted of 841 patients diagnosed with MCI at their first visit (baseline).

candidate_explanations.difference: Data processing: TADPOLE aggregates ADNI editions that may have been processed differently.
candidate_explanations.quote: the TADPOLE Challenge data were aggregated from multiple editions of ADNI (1, 2 and GO), which may have been processed in distinct ways

reason: Both studies predict MCI-to-AD/dementia progression in ADNI from cognitive and MRI data. P-168's longitudinal AUC 0.93 and, on the matched single-timepoint input, 0.90 both lie outside the interval derived for P-156's 0.81, and 0.81 lies outside P-168's intervals. The differences in horizon, cohort construction, timepoint, feature set, validation and label could produce the gap, but they are not shown to be sufficient: P-168 quantifies only the longitudinal-input effect (0.03 of the 0.12). The result rests on a derived interval for P-156, whose test class split is not printed, and the 0.90 lies only just above that interval's upper bound (0.884).
